A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AA-2DGS work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original AA-2DGS evaluations on Blender, Mip-NeRF 360, and DTU, including quantitative component ablations in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and ablations and adds qualitative RGB and normal-rendering comparisons in Figure 5.

M1.justification: The world-space flat smoothing kernel, object-space Mip filter, ray-splat mapping, and rendering procedure remain unchanged. The added normal-rendering illustration does not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Blender, Mip-NeRF 360, and DTU coverage is retained. New Figure 5 modestly extends qualitative evaluation to normal rendering under magnification and minification, beyond the previously reported RGB rendering and mesh reconstruction.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–7 remains identical, including the 2DGS variants and reconstruction baselines. Figure 5 uses the existing 2DGS comparator; newly cited methods such as HDGS are discussed but not added to evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The documented splits, image resolutions, sampling weights, metrics, 30K training iterations, and filter settings remain unchanged. Figure 5 applies existing zoom conditions to normal rendering without specifying a distinct new training or sampling procedure.

E4.justification: Figure 5 adds a qualitative case study of whether anti-aliasing benefits extend to normals at 2× zoom-in and 4× zoom-out. The component-removal ablations in Appendix A, including Tables 6 and 7, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revised rendering-overhead range is a computational-cost report, not a new statistical uncertainty estimate.

E6.justification: Section 4.1 changes reported rendering overhead relative to 2DGS from 10–15% to 15–30%, without establishing a same-setting rerun. Figure 5 adds qualitative normal/RGB results, while Figure 4 loses two example rows. Numerical results in Tables 1–7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Equations 1–17 are retained. Changes to transpose notation, the maximum's index in Equation 8, and the multiplication symbol in Equation 10 are equivalent notation rather than revised reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same two filter contributions and claims of improved anti-aliasing across sampling rates while preserving geometric reconstruction. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly interprets the normal-rendering example as evidence of benefits beyond RGB and suggests applications to reconstruction and reflective scenes. It removes the specific qualification about GOF's superior mesh extraction. The new main-text limitations section summarizes limitations already present in v1's appendix.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 revises the documented rendering-cost overhead from 10–15% to 15–30%. CUDA implementation information, hardware, hyperparameters, and the code-access link remain unchanged; no explanation of the timing revision is added.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands literature coverage, adding 35 works on sparse/noisy reconstruction, generalizable priors, regularization, textured splatting, and newer Gaussian-splatting techniques. It also discusses HDGS's frustum-based supersampling. The original references and positioning relative to Mip-Splatting remain.

P1.justification: V2 makes terminology and grammar corrections, updates affiliations and publication text, fixes the unresolved DTU table reference, and adds a main-text limitations summary. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the RGB/normal comparison in Figure 5, reduces Figure 4 from six example rows to four, and relocates Tables 4–5. Existing appendix figures are retained and renumbered, with higher-resolution reproduction of the final row in the Mip-NeRF 360 figure.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful qualitative evidence about normal rendering, broadens related-work context, fixes a broken table reference, and makes existing limitations more prominent. These are modest improvements because the method and all benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged. Figure 4 provides fewer examples, and the broad interpretation about all rendered attributes exceeds the specific normal-rendering evidence. The higher reported runtime overhead does not establish that the algorithm itself deteriorated.
